claims.claim_text: I was on the far north side of the city at the time of the broadcast.
I observed a grey Chevrolet Suburban being pursued southbound by Officer Fuentes.
Due to damage to Officer Fuentes's vehicle from a prior attempted vehicle stop, I assumed the lead position.
At the time I became lead vehicle, the subject had been pursued with continuously activated lights and sirens for over seven minutes.
The subject turned into the Buena Park Unified School District Office parking lot, driving through the closed entry gate and dislodging it from its hinges.
The subject's vehicle collided with a parked vehicle at low speed before coming to a complete stop.
The subject remained seated inside the vehicle for approximately thirty seconds before exiting.
I observed him holding a handgun in his left hand.
I discharged my firearm thirteen times at the subject.
The subject walked toward us for several seconds while pointing his weapon before falling to the ground.
I immediately requested medical assistance via radio at 1408 hours.

It should be noted that the child passenger had already been removed from the bus prior to the shooting at the school district parking lot. W-1 had dropped the child at a school earlier on her route, and the bus was empty at the time the subject fired his weapon at it on Orangethorpe Avenue.
He was wearing a black T-shirt, blue jeans, a load bearing vest with a BPPD badge and a large cloth patch that said 'Police' on the front.
I was aware from radio traffic that the subject had fired at a school bus carrying children and that the subject was armed with a handgun.
